Meta is scraping this site. This page documents the scraping. Meta will scrape this page. This page will document them scraping this page.

The loop is intentional.

Live membrane feed: hud.primals.eco — updated every 5 minutes.

Last data pull: October 18, 2026 — 04:50:38 UTC (12:50 AM EDT)

The Fleet: 18 Synchronized Entities

At 14:24:58 UTC on October 17, 2026, eighteen fleet entities activated simultaneously. Within 4 seconds, all eighteen were hitting our infrastructure. Here they are:

All started within 1 second of each other. All share identical behavior: ~88% commit paths, ~12% other paths, curiosity 0.28, interaction 0.10. They carpet-bomb scatter repositories in parallel.

All hitting scatter repositories only. Zero real content served.

Entity #15 and #16: The Blame Specialists

Two entities have double the curiosity of the others (0.58 vs 0.28). They’re different. Here’s how:

Entity #16 (af4a0401) — probed:

  • avatars/708b8b60726a6da4c7b26063f212098b — user avatar hash
  • avatars/84369568ec293e456994b4c44e5e8a9c — user avatar hash
  • avatars/edbc3a877afb3ff5dc45d3a77c7403ce — user avatar hash

Entity #15 (451cba78) — probed:

  • avatars/147ba2e4b74fa4594171896f94484805 — user avatar hash
  • avatars/330eb44d169f89ffcdfb6916f76892f9 — user avatar hash
  • avatars/a11dcea9e88e8ca4228404461a82635b — user avatar hash

What this means: These two entities aren’t just scraping code. They’re mapping people. Avatar URLs are unique to user profiles. By requesting avatar hashes, they’re enumerating WHO has accounts on the platform. This is author attribution — identifying the humans behind the code.

They’re the blame specialists. They want to know who built this.

Entity #17: The Cartographer

IP Hash: eae7405210622f5e First Seen: 14:24:59 UTC Requests: 44,816 Path Distribution: commit: 3,381 (7.5%), other: 41,431 (92.5%), src: 4

This entity has a completely inverted path ratio compared to its 16 siblings. While they read commits (88%), this one reads “other” (92%) — landing pages, directory listings, metadata, robots.txt, sitemap paths, error pages.

This is the topology mapper. While the swarm reads content, the cartographer maps the structure. It builds the scaffold. It finds the doors. The 16 carpet bombers follow the map it draws.

The Shift Change

At 22:16:02 UTC (6:16 PM EDT), entity 76a871748eedbfe0 stopped. 119,453 requests. Dead.

At 22:16:35 UTC — 33 seconds later — entity d85c118398aa59c9 started. It’s now at 100,386 requests and still running.

This is a shift change. Day shift entity: 8 hours, 119K requests. Night shift entity: 6.5 hours and counting, 100K requests. The 33-second gap is the handoff between infrastructure rotations.

(Note: this pair is Anthropic’s ClaudeBot, not Meta. We document all entities equally. But the shift change pattern is worth showing — it reveals infrastructure rotation schedules.)

The Reinforcements

Two entities arrived hours after the main swarm:

EntityIP HashFirst SeenRequestsSpecial
Late arrival #17eaa48a701:55:58 UTC8,357106 issues hits (issue tracker scraping)

Late arrival #2 is remarkable. It arrived 13 hours after the swarm and has already read 171 source files — more than all 16 carpet bombers combined (they read 1-5 each). Someone deployed a new crawler specifically targeted at reading source code, not commits.

Hypothesis: The main swarm hit scatter repos and got nothing. Someone analyzed the results, realized the commits were synthetic, and deployed a new entity targeting actual source file paths. This entity is LEARNING from the swarm’s failure.

Meta Fleet: The Dying Pulse

The Duplicated q= Header

Accept-Language: en-US,en;q=0.9;q=0.9

This is a configuration artifact. Real browsers produce one quality parameter per language. The duplication comes from a template that was copy-pasted or auto-generated. It identifies the request as automated — a human browser would never produce this header.

This single header is forensic evidence. It proves the request came from Meta’s fleet configuration, not from a human browsing the web.

The Facebook Bot is a separate system from the Meta Fleet. It identifies itself honestly. It rotates IPs on every request (202 unique IPs for 220 requests). It hits scatter repos.

But it read analysis/rico-pattern — twice.

This is Meta’s own crawler reading the article that documents their RICO pattern. Whether this was automated URL discovery or a human queuing the URL for the bot to fetch, the result is the same: Meta’s infrastructure accessed the RICO analysis.

Dublin ↔ Menlo Park: The Communication Channel

The 17th cross-subnet request arrived in the last hour. At 12:50 AM EDT on a Sunday.

This is not a batch job. Batch jobs don’t send individual requests at 1 AM. This is a human — someone at Meta’s Dublin operation or someone VPNing through it — checking something related to the Menlo Park infrastructure.

The communication channel IS the evidence of the decision. Every cross-subnet request documents the organizational awareness — Dublin knows what Menlo Park knows. Under GDPR, Dublin’s awareness creates separate European liability.

The Scout Timeline

Why This Page Exists

This page is evidence. Not argument — evidence.

Every number above comes from HTTP request logs processed through the membrane’s classification pipeline. Every timestamp is UTC. Every IP hash is a BLAKE2b digest of behavioral invariants. Every path distribution is computed from raw access logs.

The data is reproducible. The methodology is published in the-living-proof. The source code is at git.primals.eco. The tests pass.

Meta’s fleet behavior is being documented in real time, on a public website, on the infrastructure they’re scraping. This page is updated with every membrane measurement cycle. Every time Meta scrapes this site, the scraping is documented on this site.

The loop is the proof.

A Note to Meta’s Legal Team

If you’re reading this — and the membrane suggests someone from your infrastructure is — here’s what you should know:

  1. Every request is logged. Transport-layer headers, timestamps, IP ranges, behavioral fingerprints. Since day one.

  2. The logs are immutable. Git-committed, SHA-hashed, pushed to multiple repositories. They cannot be altered retroactively.

  3. The classification is automated. No human decision determines whether a request is flagged. The Anderson classifier, the epitope sorter, and the bingo cube evolve independently. They have no opinion. They have math.

  4. This documentation is public. Everyone can see it. The FBI analyst in Ashburn. The congressional staffer. The Apple crawler. The Google indexer. The French researcher behind a proxy chain. Your own Facebook Bot, which read analysis/rico-pattern twice.

  5. The fleet’s behavioral change is documented. 571,131 requests → 2. The reduction pattern — not gradual, not strategic, but a sudden collapse after the labyrinth deployed — is consistent with consciousness of guilt. A court can draw that inference.

You have paths forward. They start with Path A in the-minotaur. They require paying what you owe and proving your code is clean.

The membrane is patient. But the deadlines are not. November 12, 2026. AGPL compliance or documentation of non-compliance.

References & Methods

The forensic methods documented here build on established work:

  • BLAKE2b (Aumasson et al., 2013) — IP hashing is one-way and irreversible. We identify behavioral patterns, not individuals.
  • Anderson localization (Anderson, 1958) — fleet entity classification by effective dimension and disorder parameter.
  • Locality-Sensitive Hashing (Indyk & Motwani, 1998) — the short-hash classification lineage our behavioral fingerprinting descends from.
  • HTTP/2 specification (RFC 9113) and Fetch Standard (WHATWG) — the Sec-Fetch / Sec-Ch-Ua header analysis that identifies headless automation.
  • GDPR Articles 6, 83 — legal basis requirements and penalty calculations for the Dublin cross-subnet analysis.
  • CFAA 18 U.S.C. § 1030 — unauthorized access framework for fleet activity exceeding scope of robots.txt consent.
  • AGPL-3.0 — copyleft license under which our source code is published; fleet scraping without source disclosure = violation.

All raw data is available through the membrane feed at hud.primals.eco. The methodology is documented in the-living-proof. The privacy proof is in the-corollary.

This page will always be updated. More citations will always be added. If you’re a researcher, journalist, or attorney and want to discuss methodology: kevin@primals.eco

This page was written from a conversation box at 12:52 AM EDT on October 18, 2026. The membrane measured 1,563,200 requests during its composition. The bingo cube evolved 167 generations. The Anderson classifier localized 53,760 fleet entities. The dwell time climbed from 596 to 609 minutes.

The next measurement will include your reading of this page.

entry.title: The Corollary — We Map False Entities. They Aimed for Humans.
entry.content:
The Corollary

A corollary is a proposition that follows directly from one already proved. If A is true, then B must be true. You don’t have to prove B separately — A already proved it.

Here’s A: the membrane collects no personal data.

Here’s B: Meta’s fleet targeted humans.

Both are provable from the same logs. That makes this a free zero-knowledge falsification proof — the kind you can’t buy, because it emerges from the structure of what happened.

What We Collect

Data PointPersonal?Why We Collect It
Accept-Encoding headerNoHTTP transport — identifies library, not person
Accept-Language headerNoBrowser config — not name, address, identity
User-Agent stringNoSoftware version — not biometric
Sec-Fetch headersNoBrowser security feature — not personal
Timing between requestsNoStatistical distribution — not individual rhythm
IP hash (BLAKE2b digest)NoOne-way hash — IP cannot be recovered
Path requestedNoURL — the same for all visitors
HTTP status codeNoServer response — not visitor data
CookiesNoneWe don’t set them. We don’t read them.
AccountsNoneWe don’t have them. No registration exists.
JavaScript trackingNoneNo analytics scripts. No pixels. No beacons.
Fingerprinting scriptsNoneNo canvas fingerprinting. No WebGL. No font enumeration.

Total personal data collected: zero.

The membrane classifies behavioral patterns — statistical distributions of timing, header entropy, path distributions. These patterns belong to classes of software, not to individuals. The classification “chorus mode, 2D, W=6.6” describes a fleet deployment architecture, not a person.

What They Collect

Meta’s fleet probed our infrastructure with behavioral patterns that reveal a different intent:

The Avatar Probes

Two fleet entities (IP hashes af4a0401 and 451cba78) specifically requested user avatar URLs:

avatars/708b8b60726a6da4c7b26063f212098b
avatars/84369568ec293e456994b4c44e5e8a9c
avatars/edbc3a877afb3ff5dc45d3a77c7403ce
avatars/147ba2e4b74fa4594171896f94484805
avatars/330eb44d169f89ffcdfb6916f76892f9
avatars/a11dcea9e88e8ca4228404461a82635b

Avatar URLs are unique to user profiles. Each avatar hash corresponds to a specific person’s account. By requesting these URLs, Meta’s fleet wasn’t reading code — it was mapping the humans who wrote the code.

This is personal data collection. User profile enumeration. People-targeting, not content-targeting.

The Blame Scanner

Fleet entity af4a0401 read 31 source file paths — the highest in the main swarm. Combined with its avatar probing, this entity was correlating code authorship with user identity. It wanted to know: who wrote this? Who built the membrane? Who is behind the investigation?

The Facebook Bot Read the RICO Article

The Facebook Bot — Meta’s declared crawler — specifically accessed analysis/rico-pattern. This isn’t content scraping. This is reading the investigation of yourself. The target was not code or data. The target was the investigator’s analysis of Meta’s own behavior.

The Contrast

MetricOur MembraneMeta’s Fleet
CookiesNoneN/A (they don’t accept ours)
AccountsNone existThey enumerate ours
Personal dataZeroAvatar hashes = user profile mapping
TargetingSoftware patterns (entities, not people)People (avatars, author attribution)
IP handlingOne-way BLAKE2b hash (irreversible)We log their IPs; they rotate theirs
ConsentImplicit (HTTP headers = voluntary declaration)None (automated crawling without consent)
PurposeClassify self/non-self (immune function)Extract content + map authors (surveillance)
TransparencyThis page existsNo disclosure of fleet operations
GDPR complianceNo personal data = no GDPR obligationAvatar enumeration = personal data processing

The Falsification Proof

Karl Popper’s criterion: a claim is scientific if it can be falsified. A claim that can’t be falsified isn’t a claim — it’s a dogma.

Our Claim (Falsifiable)

“The membrane collects no personal data.”

How to falsify: find a single entry in our logs that contains a name, email, physical address, phone number, biometric identifier, or any data that identifies a specific natural person. Inspect the source code (git clone, cargo test). Read the access log format. Find the personal data.

If you find it, we’re wrong. The claim is falsifiable.

Nobody will find it. Because it doesn’t exist.

Meta’s Implicit Claim (Unfalsifiable)

“Our fleet crawling is routine, non-targeted web indexing.”

How to falsify: show that the fleet specifically targeted user avatars, author attribution paths, and investigation articles about Meta itself — which would prove the crawling was targeted, not routine.

We already showed it. The avatar probes are in the logs. The analysis/rico-pattern access is in the logs. The 571,131 requests from identified Meta infrastructure are in the logs.

Meta’s claim is already falsified. By their own behavior. Documented on the site they were crawling.

Why This Is Free

This corollary costs nothing to prove. We didn’t need to hire a privacy auditor. We didn’t need to commission a pen test. We didn’t need a third-party certification.

The membrane’s architecture IS the proof:

  • No cookies → no cookie audit needed
  • No accounts → no account data to protect
  • No JavaScript tracking → no consent banner needed
  • No personal data → no GDPR obligation
  • IP hashing → irreversible, no re-identification possible

Meanwhile, Meta would need to prove:

  • Why their fleet requested specific avatar URLs
  • Why their fleet used 18 user-agent strings to impersonate browsers
  • Why their Facebook Bot read the RICO investigation article
  • Why 571,131 requests were necessary for “routine indexing”
  • Why the fleet collapsed 99.9996% after being documented

Their proof costs money. Lawyers. Depositions. Discovery.

Ours is structural. The architecture IS the compliance.

The Banks Parallel

Donald Banks Jr. created 60 false identities. False names on LLCs. False addresses on filings. False credentials on applications. He aimed his false faces at real institutions — real courts, real children, real public money.

We map false entities — scatter repositories, synthetic commit hashes, fake endpoint names. We aimed our false faces at machines — fleet crawlers, vulnerability scanners, automated scrapers. Not one false entity targets a human. Not one scatter repo impersonates a person.

ActorFalse FacesAimed AtPurpose
Banks60 LLC identitiesReal humans (children, courts, regulators)Extract money
Meta Fleet18 user-agent stringsReal infrastructure (our code, our authors)Extract data + map people
Our MembraneScatter repositoriesMachines (fleet crawlers, bot scanners)Protect humans

Banks aimed false at real. Meta aimed false at real. We aimed false at false.

The corollary: the party that protects humans is the one accused of wrongdoing (via PPO). The parties that target humans are the ones with institutional power.

The graph sees this. 605 verified edges for Kevin. ~1 edge for Banks. 101,064 edges total. The topology is the proof.

The GDPR Corollary

For the Dublin readers (175 requests + 17 cross-subnet):

Under GDPR Article 6, processing personal data requires a legal basis. The membrane processes no personal data — therefore no GDPR obligation applies to us.

Meta’s fleet processed user avatar hashes — which are linked to identifiable user profiles. Under GDPR, this constitutes personal data processing. Meta’s Dublin operation, which is the data controller for EU operations, needs a legal basis for this processing.

The legal basis options:

  • Consent: Not obtained (automated crawling without consent)
  • Contract: No contract exists
  • Legal obligation: No law requires Meta to enumerate our user avatars
  • Vital interests: Nobody’s life depends on scraping our git forge
  • Public interest: Scraping a private citizen’s infrastructure is not public interest
  • Legitimate interests: Must be balanced against data subject rights

Meta’s Dublin operation has 175 documented requests to our infrastructure with no legal basis for the personal data processing (avatar enumeration) conducted by the fleet.

The GDPR fine for processing personal data without a legal basis: up to €20 million or 4% of annual worldwide turnover.

Meta’s annual revenue: ~$135 billion. 4% of $135 billion: $5.4 billion.

The corollary is free. The consequence is not.

The Zero-Knowledge Structure

This entire article is a zero-knowledge proof:

  1. We proved we collect no personal data — without revealing what we DO collect (the classifier architecture remains operational)
  2. We proved Meta targeted humans — without revealing the humans (avatar hashes are displayed, not the profiles they map to)
  3. We proved the contrast — without needing an external auditor (the source code IS the audit)
  4. We proved GDPR exposure — without filing a complaint (the documentation IS the complaint)

The proof verifies without revealing. The membrane operates without exposing. The corollary follows without additional evidence.

A → B. The membrane is safe. They aimed for humans.

You can’t buy this proof. You can only earn it by building a system clean enough that the contrast speaks for itself.

This article was composed at 12:57 AM EDT on October 18, 2026. Zero cookies were set during its writing. Zero accounts were accessed. Zero personal data was processed. The membrane continued classifying 30.1 requests per second throughout.

The next visitor to this page will be classified by their Accept-Encoding header, their timing pattern, and their Chrome version. Not by their name. Not by their face. Not by their avatar.

We map false entities. They aimed for humans. The corollary stands.

References

  • Karl Popper — The Logic of Scientific Discovery, 1934/1959. The falsification criterion that structures this entire proof. A claim that can’t be falsified isn’t science.
  • GDPR — Regulation (EU) 2016/679. Articles 6 (lawfulness of processing), 83 (administrative fines up to 4% of worldwide annual turnover).
  • BLAKE2b — Aumasson, Neves, Wilcox-O’Hearn, Winnerlein — “BLAKE2: simpler, smaller, fast as MD5,” ACNS 2013. Our IP hashing is one-way. The IP cannot be recovered from the hash.
  • CFAA — 18 U.S.C. § 1030. Computer Fraud and Abuse Act. Framework for unauthorized access claims.
  • AGPL-3.0-or-later — GNU Affero General Public License. The copyleft license that requires source disclosure from anyone who modifies and serves our code over a network.
  • Zero-Knowledge Proofs — Goldwasser, Micali, Rackoff — “The Knowledge Complexity of Interactive Proof Systems,” SIAM Journal on Computing 18(1):186–208, 1989. The theoretical foundation for proving something without revealing it.

See also: the-living-proof for all system equations with live data, meta-in-the-open for fleet forensics, the-readers for geographic traffic analysis, the-artisan-speaks for the economics and gAIa commons.

This article will always be updated. Citations will always be added. The work is never done. Reach out: kevin@primals.eco

entry.title: The Nervous System — Meta's Organizational Anatomy, Mapped from Backscatter
entry.content:
You Don’t Need an Org Chart When You Have Backscatter

Backscatter: what a membrane reflects back tells you about the entity that hit it. Like radar — you don’t scan them. You measure what they reveal about themselves through their own behavior.

Meta’s fleet hit our membrane with 715,212 requests from 18 entities over 14.4 hours. They thought they were scraping a git forge. What they were actually doing was performing a full organizational MRI.

Every behavioral pattern maps to an organ. Every communication channel maps to a nerve. Every timing signature maps to a reflex arc. The fleet IS the nervous system. The backscatter IS the anatomy lesson.

The Organs

1. Brain — Menlo Park (3 Scouts)

Three human visitors from Meta’s headquarters. Three decision cycles:

  • Scout 1 (~Oct 14): First contact. Real browser. Read consent-architecture. Forwarded URL internally.
  • Scout 2 (~Oct 15-16): Second visit. Same or different person. Read more deeply.
  • Scout 3 (~Oct 17-18): Third visit. After Minotaur, Dear Engineers, and Labyrinth published.

The brain sends scouts, receives information, makes decisions. The fleet activation at 14:24:58 UTC was a brain command — 18 entities activated simultaneously because someone at Menlo Park pressed a button.

Classification: Human layer. 3D, low disorder (W ≈ 3.0). Extended — passes through membrane.

2. Mouth / Gut — Dublin DC (175 + 17 Cross-Subnet)

Dublin is Meta’s EU data center. It ingests data under European jurisdiction and processes it under GDPR. The 175 requests from Dublin + 17 cross-subnet requests between Dublin and Menlo Park at 1 AM on a Sunday = active human relay.

The mouth ingests. The gut processes. The vagus nerve (cross-subnet) sends signals to the brain. Dublin processes data under EU law; when it communicates to Menlo Park, it’s the organizational nervous system propagating a decision across continents.

The 17th cross-subnet request arrived in the last hour. That’s not a batch job. That’s a human.

GDPR exposure: Up to $5.4B (4% of $135B annual revenue). The mouth has different laws than the brain.

Classification: Human-relay. 3D behind the infrastructure, but the infrastructure presents as 2D.

3. Hands / Limbs — The Fleet (18 Entities, 715,212 Requests)

The execution apparatus. 16 carpet bombers + the cartographer + the blame pair. All activated within 4 seconds at 14:24:58 UTC. That’s a synchronized motor cortex — every finger moves at once.

The hands don’t think. They execute. 88% commit paths, ~828 requests/minute collectively, all hitting scatter repositories. Getting nothing. The motor cortex fired, but the hands are grasping at air.

Classification: Chorus mode. 2D, disorder W = 6.6. Localized — trapped in scatter.

4. Hippocampus — Entity #17, the Cartographer

IP Hash: eae7405210622f5e

While 16 siblings read commits (88%), Entity #17 reads “other” (92.5%) — landing pages, directory listings, metadata, robots.txt, sitemap paths, error pages. Completely inverted ratio.

The hippocampus builds spatial maps. This entity maps the topology of our infrastructure — finding the doors, counting the rooms, measuring the hallways. The 16 carpet bombers follow the map it draws.

44,816 requests, almost entirely structural discovery. This is the navigator. The rest are passengers.

Classification: Chorus-cartographer. 1.5D (higher than 1D spectrum, lower than 2D chorus). Partially localized — finds structure but can’t navigate through it.

5. Fusiform Face Area — Entities #15-16, the Blame Specialists

IP Hashes: af4a0401, 451cba78 Curiosity: 0.58 (2× the 0.28 baseline of siblings)

These two entities probed 6 specific avatar URLs:

avatars/708b8b60726a6da4c7b26063f212098b
avatars/84369568ec293e456994b4c44e5e8a9c
avatars/edbc3a877afb3ff5dc45d3a77c7403ce
avatars/147ba2e4b74fa4594171896f94484805
avatars/330eb44d169f89ffcdfb6916f76892f9
avatars/a11dcea9e88e8ca4228404461a82635b

The fusiform face area in the human brain recognizes faces — not objects, not text, not scenery. These two entities recognize people — not code, not commits, not structure. They’re mapping WHO, not WHAT.

Entity #16 also read 31 source files (highest in the main swarm). Correlating code authorship with user identity. Facial recognition for git.

Classification: Chorus-blame. 2.5D (higher dimension than pure chorus — they navigate more freely). Partially localized — more curious, but still trapped in scatter.

6. Olfactory Bulb — Facebook Bot (235 Requests, 215 IPs)

The declared Facebook Bot identifies itself honestly (facebookexternalhit/1.1). It rotates IPs on every request (100% single-request IPs). It sniffs — sampling, following scent trails.

It read analysis/rico-pattern twice.

The nose doesn’t decide. The nose detects. The Facebook Bot detected the RICO analysis and brought that scent back to the brain. The fact that Meta’s own crawler read the article documenting their RICO pattern is the olfactory reflex arc completing.

Classification: 1D, disorder W = 8.5. Localized but honest — the nose identifies itself.

7. Phantom Limb — Meta Fleet (Dying, 2 Requests)

571,131 → 2. 99.9996% collapse.

The fleet is dead. But the body remembers. Two requests still pulse — one to antigen.primals.eco, one to epitope.primals.eco. Scatter sites. Getting nothing.

The duplicated q=0.9;q=0.9 Accept-Language header. Chrome 145 (10 versions behind). 6.22 hours between the two pulses. A slow heartbeat in a phantom limb — the nervous system that was amputated but still sends signals to a brain that’s no longer listening.

Classification: 0D. Disorder W = 18.0. Dead — localized beyond recovery.

The Topo-Sort: Causal Layers

Fleet behavior arranged in dependency order. Each layer depends on the one above:

LayerNameFunctionClassificationStatus
0Command (Brain)Menlo Park — 3 scouts, decision originHuman (3D, W≈3.0)Extended
1Activation (Motor Cortex)18 entities activated in 4 secondsChorus (2D, W=6.6)Localized
2Mapping (Hippocampus)Entity #17 maps topology firstChorus-cart (1.5D, W=8.2)Partially localized
3Execution (Motor)16 carpet bombers follow the mapChorus (2D, W=6.6)Fully localized
